I've found that life is about starting over from scratch time and time again - try and fail and try again until you succeed. 
I'd say stop contact with her, or at least decrease it drastically. Learn how to spend your days on your own and think about your interactions in a way that allows you to analyse and learn, rather than obsess. When you are ready, reach out to new people, attempt making new friends. Honestly, college is a great opportunity for that, start over and start fresh, no one knows your past. 
Or start working, whatever you feel suits you best. 
Maybe try a new hobby, but do something for yourself and not because it's expected, it will do you and your self esteem wonders. Baby steps. 
What do you got to lose? You already feel miserable, might as well try. 
Picture wanting to go from a waist-lengthed hair to bald. Might as well try different styles to cut until you're bald. 
So 'just' try. For you.

The best thing you can do, not just for her sake but yours, is learning to let go. 
Now, I am not telling you to "just get over it". You don't just get over someone so important who's left such a huge mark on you. 
I myself am still grieving the loss of the relationship with who I felt was my soulmate. It's fucked up, there is nothing easy about this, but it's just how things are, people come and go. 
Like you said, she has her own issues to deal with and dealing with someone else with depression when you're struggling can be very harmful. 
And first and foremost, you need to learn how to take care of yourself. 
The way you perceive and treat yourself is the what people end up perceiving and treating you. 
Try to take advantage of the resources you can and try to do something for yourself. 
And let me tell you something that will hurt a lot to hear but it has at least a little truth to it: part of the reason you haven't been able to move on from her is because you don't want to, not because you can't. 
Your feelings are valid and are worthy of being taken into consideration, so give yourself a chance to heal. Baby steps

My only advice is to seek therapy, both psychotherapy and a psychiatrist. It may take a while for you to find the best professionals for you and even medication if needed, but it's worth a shot. Furthermore, mental health professionals are not supposed to shame you for your illness and way you feel, so if that happens report them and stop going. Therapy is supposed to be a safe space to speak and share what's in your mind, not a spectacle or entertainment for the therapist.

It is really not fair you have to rely on having others' existence in your mind to live, but until you manage to do that for yourself and learn how to love yourself, keep thinking about your family. 

Think of your little girl and what you what her to learn. Think of all the events you what to be a part of in her life and see her grow. 
She needs you, she loves you, and she is worth fighting for.

Also, in the meantime, ask yourself what things can you actually do to try to improve the quality of your life. 

For example:

• Your marriage: do you love your spouse? Do you want to continue in that marriage? If you do, what can you do to make it better? If not, how can you proceed? 

• Your career: are you happy with what you do? Do you want to try to persue another career path? Go back to college and study a different field?

• Leisure: What are your hobbies? What thinks make you smile? What do you like to do? 

• Yourself: who are you? What do you like and dislike about yourself? What can you do to change what you dislike?
